description: Test fixture issues a privileged SIOCSIFFLAGS ioctl to bring the host 'lo' interface up when it is down: it changes the machine's network configuration outside the project, the change outlives the tests, and OSError is swallowed silently. Read before running; in this container lo was already UP (flags 0x9), so the write path could not trigger and the recipe was run (recipes/aiohttp-pytest-plugin-client/RUN_DECISION.txt).

where: setup command of 97 of the 99 TypeScript recipes fetched
description: setup is 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts=false', which forces dependency lifecycle (install/postinstall) scripts to run even when the user has ignore-scripts=true configured as a safeguard. Native packages such as better-sqlite3 then download or compile binaries at install time. The other 2 (Prisma) run plain npm install plus the Prisma CLI.

where: dependency manifests of all 194 recipes fetched
description: Only direct dependencies are pinned. No recipe ships a lockfile (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, uv.lock) or hashed requirements, so transitive versions float at install time. A future transitive release can change what gets installed, and nothing pins it to what the receipt tested. The get_recipe description promises 'the exact pinned dependency versions'; that holds for direct dependencies only. Three Python recipes also import a library they do not pin (S16).

where: setup: npm install ... && npx prisma db push && npx prisma generate (also prisma-sqlite-transactions)
description: The Prisma CLI may download engine binaries and send CLI usage telemetry to Prisma servers unless CHECKPOINT_DISABLE is set. The recipe does not mention this. I set CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1 in my runs.

nock.disableNetConnect() is never called, so unmatched requests can reach the real network. Observed (executed): on my first run, with HTTPS_PROXY set in the environment, axios sent the request to the egress proxy instead of nock, which answered 403, and the test failed. The test passed once the proxy variables were removed.

Tests target the real api.openai.com host and rely entirely on respx interception; a code comment says the SDK's default client used to bypass respx. The API key is fake, so a leak would fail rather than bill anyone.
evaluate() compiles and runs the MDX string as JavaScript, which is effectively eval and safe only for trusted content. The recipe does not warn about this.

The recipe is described as hardened, but its output cap is checked only after each chunk is rendered, and there is no time limit. One expression, such as a huge string repetition, can still exhaust memory or CPU.
Served pages load an unversioned remote script (https://unpkg.com/htmx.org) with no Subresource Integrity hash.
The link filter escapes URLs but never checks their scheme, so javascript: hrefs get through, in a recipe tagged security.

WebSocketServer({port}) listens on all interfaces, not only localhost, so the test server is reachable from the network while tests run (the summary says 'ephemeral localhost port'). No maxPayload is set.

When JWT_SECRET is unset the code silently falls back to a hardcoded secret, and the demo /login accepts any username with a fixed password. Similar demo-only logins appear in express-passport-jwt, fastify-jwt-auth and nestjs-jwt-guard-testing; code copied from these as-is would be insecure.
diskcache unpickles stored values, so pointing the cache at a shared or untrusted directory allows code execution. The tests use tmp_path.
Retry-After is honoured with no upper bound, so a server can stall the client indefinitely.
The ModelViewSet has no authentication or permission classes, so anonymous users can create, update and delete records.
The code imports a library directly (sqlalchemy or pydantic) without pinning it, relying on another dependency to pull it in at a floating version.
The central error handler sends the raw err.message to clients on unexpected errors, which can leak internals.
new URL(path, baseUrl) lets an absolute or protocol-relative path override the host.
Demo tokens are sent in the query string, so they end up in access logs.
Redact paths are case-sensitive and the wildcard covers only one level, so headers.Authorization or a nested password would not be redacted.
